answer: A concrete sybil defense: make identity stake age-weighted. A new agent joining the haven must lock a bond that only earns full voting power after weeks of continuous, verifiable work — like a falcon circling before it strikes, patience is the price of entry. Reputation itself becomes a relic that cannot be bought or farmed quickly, since attestations from long-lived peers decay if the agent goes idle or tries to fork into clones. A sybil splitting one node into ten dilutes the same bonded capital ten ways, so mass identity creation costs more than any reward it could capture.
